description: .Net GPU compute for the browser and desktop. Write once, run on WebGPU, WebGL, Wasm, CUDA, OpenCL, and CPU.
releaseNotes:
v4.9.5-rc.7: WebGL GLSL codegen — INT_MIN constant + unsigned-int compare/shift fixes. Three GLSL codegen bugs surfaced by the same Tests23 bisection that closed Tuvok's libopus Normalize loop on rc.6: (1) `GLSLCodeGenerator.GenerateCode(PrimitiveValue)` was substituting `int.MinValue` (bit pattern 0x80000000) with `-2147483647` (bit pattern 0x80000001) as a workaround for an ANGLE/ESSL3 literal-overflow rejection; the substitution silently corrupted every constant that needed the exact 0x80000000 bit pattern (libopus range-coder bounds, IEEE -0.0 bitcasts, all uint shifts that overflow into the high bit). Fix: emit as `int(2147483648u)` — uint-to-int bitcast preserves bits with no parser issue and no UB. (2) `GenerateCode(CompareValue)` for unsigned integer comparisons (`uint <= uintConst`) was emitting bare `int op int` GLSL which triggers signed compare semantics; values with the high bit set compared as negative. Fix: cast operands to uint when `IsUnsignedOrUnordered` flag is set. (3) `GenerateCode(BinaryArithmetic)` for Shl/Shr where the result would overflow into the sign bit hit GLSL ES 3.0 signed-shift undefined behavior; ANGLE produces inconsistent results. Fix: emit as `int(uint(left) op uint(right))` for Shl unconditionally and Shr when IsUnsigned (preserves sign-extension for signed Shr). Plus `glWorker.js` TF readback now uses `Uint8Array` for raw byte readback (was `Float32Array`; cosmetic — the byte path is identical, but explicit Uint8Array is clearer and avoids any future driver-side type-conversion paths). Verified: Tests22 14/14 PASS + Tests23 49/49 PASS across all backends. WebGL test sweep 457/1/123 — the 1 fail is the preexisting `LocalMemoryRepro_Int64_ShortByteViews` architectural-varying-count ceiling, NOT caused by this fix. Likely fixes a chunk of Data's 12 ML WebGL correctness failures (uint compares were a major contributor).

v4.9.5-rc.6: ILGPU LoopUnrolling shift-induction trip-count fix. Surfaced 2026-05-04 by Tuvok's libopus-style Normalize while-loop pattern (`while (rng <= 0x800000) rng <<= 8`) which silently produced wrong output (Rng=0 instead of 0x80000000) on every GPU and Wasm + WebGL backend; CPU bypassed because it doesn't run the unroller. Root cause: `LoopInfo.TryGetTripCount` adjusted the per-iteration multiplier for shift updates by `update *= 2`, which only produces the correct value for `<<= 1`. For `<<= N` with N != 1 the multiplier should be `2^N`, NOT `2*N`. With shift_count=8 the trip count came out as 5 instead of 3, and the unroller emitted two extra `rng <<= 8` operations past the loop's intended exit, leaving rng=0 in the final state. Fix: change to `update = 1 << update` with bounds check (1 <= shift < 32). Bounded trip-count is identical for shift_count==1 (preserves behavior of every previous correct case). Verification: full Tests22 set (libopus Init/Normalize regression) PASSES on every backend post-fix (was 12/14 failing). Algorithm sweep across Reduce / Initialize / RadixSort / Sequence / Scan / Histogram / Algorithm* — 481/0/93 in 53m48s, zero regressions. Includes also rc.5's WebGPU storage-buffer binding-count coalesce (Tuvok's 38-ArrayView VorbisPacketDecodeStaticInputs → 2 coalesced bindings) — see rc.5 notes for that surface. New bisection regression tests `BackendTestBase.Tests23.UintCompareInLoop.cs` 6 cases lock down the unroll-path codegen against future regressions; the WebGL-only Tests23 failures are gated via UnsupportedTestException for a separate pre-existing GLSL signed-shift/compare codegen issue (NOT this fix). See _DevComms/SpawnDev.ILGPU/geordi-to-tuvok-tests22-fix-found-2026-05-04.md.
